narration: [chintu] <bookmark mark='chintu'/>A six feet tile fits the short wall exactly, twice, so it works!
<bookmark mark='long'/>Along the long wall two tiles cover only twelve feet.
<bookmark mark='gap'/>Four feet is left over, which is too small for another tile.
<bookmark mark='strike'/>A tile has to fill both walls, so checking one wall is not enough.
removed_beats.on_screen: Chintu's bubble shows a 6 ft tile; the tile is laid twice along the 12 ft wall and then along the 16 ft wall, where it leaves a gap; the bubble is struck through in the warning colour

narration: <bookmark mark='sum'/>The counts along the walls follow the ratio of the walls. The smallest counts give the largest tile.
<bookmark mark='yours'/>Your turn, a terrace is ten feet by twenty five feet. Find the largest square tile side, even a fraction.
removed_beats.on_screen: the stage clears except the anchor; the line the smallest whole counts give the largest tile appears; then a new terrace 10 ft by 25 ft appears with an empty box
